analysis:
Only BASE text of CBv2OwnedRequestState.swift and a truncated patch excerpt were supplied. The excerpt shows a new `submit(tokenCount:check:forward:)` at head lines ~308-349 (a second head range at 851-921 is not visible at all). The patch is cut off at `try evaluatio...`, so the commit logic is unseen.

Observed behavior of `submit`: it is an `asyncEval` variant of `run`. It refuses non-paged or packed storage. It keeps the same `requireOpen` and capacity/reservation guards and the same recurrent bind/evaluate staging. It calls `validateState(storageViews: false)`, so the commit relies on host-side frontier and binding checks instead of device-evaluated values. It has no `validateOutput` parameter, and native errors and output values surface only when the caller later reads or evaluates the output. The comment says the request fails there.

Security relevance (TB-007, T-041 and the isolation of A-001 across requests/lanes): the risk is that a step is committed (recurrent `commit`, `committedTokens` advance, `finishStep`) before native errors or the output validation surface. A later failure must mark the request failed and retire it, so partially advanced KV or recurrent state is never reused, adopted, or donated to the prefix cache. The base `run` ordering (eval, `check()`, `validateOutput`, then commit) is weakened by design. Base `retire` and `deinit` still discard failed state, and `isFailed` blocks reuse via `requireOpen`.

Integration questions for the next pass:
(1) Does the `TensorParallelOneTokenLoop` caller always evaluate or read under `MLX.withError` and call `retire(failed: true)` on any error?
(2) Can a submitted-but-unevaluated step be donated to the SSD prefix cache or handed off as a layer-stage frontier before its values are verified?
(3) What does the truncated tail of `submit` do, and what is in head range 851-921?
No concrete regression can be asserted from the visible evidence.
